title: EffectSlice: Eligibility-Gated Certificates for Task-Local Procedural Effects
hook: A validated paper effect on one locked task may admit a dependency-relative locally irreducible procedural slice, but only after the complete artifact itself clears a sealed beneficial-effect gate. EffectSlice certifies that slice against the complete artifact's paired net effect, contract, and guardrails without claiming that its search or local irreducibility criterion is new.
hook_shape_rationale: This is counter-intuitive minimalism: relative to the complete eligible artifact, the candidate executes fewer preregistered procedural atoms while preserving the same sealed task-local effect within a fixed margin. A surprising empirical reveal was rejected because existing tasks are development evidence only; the admission test must be passed on at least four genuinely new held-out paper-task pairs.

gap_closure.gap: Under a limited initial budget, no retrieved frontier establishes that the observed low-fidelity score preserves the sign and ordering of paper interventions by the performance improvement they later produce on independently specified user tasks; a probe can therefore support the wrong go/no-go decision even when it is internally faithful.
gap_closure.how_closed: Closed by defining a fixed-atomization constrained subset object whose faithfulness criterion is sealed paired equivalence to a complete artifact that first proves a beneficial effect on the same locked task.

gap_closure.gap: No retrieved frontier estimates net benefit after execution cost, adaptation effort, and regressions on task dimensions outside the paper's headline metric are deducted from gross performance gain.
gap_closure.how_closed: Closed by making cost-adjusted paired effect, contract validity, and guardrail noninferiority simultaneous fields of the same sealed source-grounded certificate rather than independent scores or a predicted utility.

core_mechanism: For one paper p and locked user task tau, EffectSlice preregisters task cases and weights, a same-scaffold no-skill baseline B, the complete PaperToSkill artifact F, primary scorer m in [0,1], guardrail scorers r_j in [0,1], GPU/API/labor conversion weights, beneficial-effect threshold delta_min, effect-equivalence margin epsilon, guardrail margins eta_j, error budgets alpha_F, alpha_D, and alpha_C, maximum adaptive queries Q=24, and maximum dependency atoms N=16. Before any slice search, a sealed eligibility pool runs paired F and B branches on three seeds; F is eligible only when its contract and guardrails pass and the preregistered one-sided lower confidence bound for its cost- and regression-adjusted paired effect Delta_tau(F) exceeds delta_min, otherwise the only output is no_validated_beneficial_effect. Atomization is frozen before outcomes: each initial node is one source-map procedure step crossed with one executable instruction or file region and one task-contract role, nodes inside the same control/data-dependency strongly connected component are merged, no atom may cross a source anchor or contract role, and the certified scope excludes task manifests, scorers, base-agent code, model weights, and paper implementation internals outside the generated skill; tasks producing more than 16 atoms return granularity_out_of_scope. A candidate S is a subset of those atoms that is source-valid, dependency-closed, executable, and contract-passing, and its one-atom neighbor S minus_dep o removes retained atom o together with every reverse-dependent atom required to restore dependency closure, so local irreducibility is explicitly relative to this atomization and dependency policy. On paired branches, z_ir(A) is the primary-score change of artifact A relative to B minus preregistered GPU, API, labor, and guardrail-regression penalties, Delta_tau(A) is the weighted mean of z_ir(A), G_tau(S)=Delta_tau(S)-Delta_tau(F), and I_tau(S) is a simultaneous interval for G_tau(S). The load-bearing effect-preservation margin is M_tau(S)=epsilon-sup{|g|: g in I_tau(S)}; a candidate can pass only when M_tau(S)>0, every contract passes, and every guardrail difference from F clears its eta_j noninferiority bound. The certified object Cert_tau(S) contains the frozen atomization policy and granularity scope, source anchors and hashes, F eligibility record, M_tau(S), contract and guardrail verdicts, run hashes, adaptive query log, and failed-removal evidence for every retained dependency atom. An interchangeable subset worker may use dependency-aware delta debugging, program slicing, branch-and-bound, or greedy deletion, maintains an accepted frontier, revisits rejected blocks after accepted deletions, and performs a complete dependency-relative one-atom scan; these search procedures, equivalence tests, one-deletion minimality, and provenance machinery are baselines or infrastructure and are not novelty claims. During discovery, query q is chosen as an F_{q-1}-measurable function of prior discovery outcomes before its fresh two-seed paired S/F/B block is revealed, and it receives alpha_q=alpha_D/[q(q+1)]; source or contract feedback may restore invalid dependencies, but effect failures may not change epsilon, scorers, atomization, or the task. The selected slice and all retained-atom deletion neighbors are then rerun on five untouched confirmation seeds, with Holm-corrected two-one-sided equivalence and guardrail-noninferiority tests at alpha_C; S_star is certified dependency-relative one-deletion-minimal only if Cert_tau(S_star) passes and every S_star minus_dep o fails at least one corrected condition, otherwise the worker returns not_certified_locally_irreducible; the only proposed novelty is the source-grounded, full-effect-eligibility-gated, sealed task-local effect-preservation certificate and worker contract that binds the fixed artifact units to direct downstream effect, with no claim to a globally minimal subset, cross-task transfer, cross-paper ranking, novel search, novel equivalence testing, novel provenance, or novel deletion criterion.
core_mechanism_reasoning: Both gaps share Cert_tau(S): the first needs a faithful subset object tied to the complete artifact's actual task effect, while the second needs the same object's cost and guardrail terms rather than another utility model. I retained the fixed-artifact subset-measurement recipe because it supplies explicit atom units, a faithfulness constraint, bounded tractability, and a sealed causal-statistical certificate rather than an operator substitution, solver-delegation architecture, or confound benchmark. Delta debugging, program slicing, prompt pruning, equivalence tests, source provenance, and dependency-relative one-deletion minimality remain mandatory baselines, not contributions.
core_mechanism_steps:
1. Freeze tau's cases, case weights, task scorer, guardrails, task contract, B, F, delta_min, epsilon, eta_j, cost weights, alpha_F/alpha_D/alpha_C, Q=24, and all seed pools; output an immutable certification manifest.
2. Run F and B on three sealed eligibility seeds and compute the preregistered lower bound for Delta_tau(F); output no_validated_beneficial_effect unless F passes contract/guardrails and the lower bound exceeds delta_min.
3. Parse the source map and generated skill into procedure-step by executable-region by contract-role nodes, merge control/data-dependency strongly connected components, and output the frozen dependency graph or granularity_out_of_scope when it exceeds 16 atoms.
4. Materialize the full dependency-closed atom set as the initial S, verify every source anchor and executable region, and output the reference atom inventory with hashes.
5. Ask an interchangeable search backend for a dependency-closed deletion candidate using only the accepted frontier and prior discovery log; output S_q before revealing its fresh seed block.
6. Execute S_q, F, and B on two fresh paired discovery seeds, update I_tau(S_q) with alpha_q=alpha_D/[q(q+1)], and record effect, contract, guardrail, resource, and artifact evidence in Cert_tau(S_q).
7. Accept a deletion only when M_tau(S_q)>0 and all contract and guardrail constraints pass; use typed source/contract feedback only to restore invalid dependencies, never to change margins, scorers, or atomization.
8. Revisit rejected blocks after every accepted deletion, test interaction neighborhoods within Q, and retain multiple passing frontiers when deletions are non-monotone.
9. Perform the complete dependency-relative one-atom scan on the chosen frontier; if Q cannot cover it, output not_certified_locally_irreducible rather than a local irreducibility claim.
10. Lock S_star and every S_star minus_dep o before opening five confirmation seeds, then rerun S_star, F, B, all retained-atom deletion neighbors, and the preregistered baselines.
11. Apply Holm-corrected two-one-sided effect-equivalence and guardrail-noninferiority tests, recompute M_tau on confirmation data, and emit a certificate only when S_star passes and every dependency-relative deletion neighbor fails.
12. Develop on the eight existing tasks, freeze the worker, and evaluate at least four genuinely new paper-task pairs separately against Graph-of-Skills-style dependency closure, semantic compact-context selection, ClawTrace-style cost-aware pruning, size-matched random selection, and generic delta-debugging backends.
falsification_prediction: After development on the existing eight tasks, freeze atomization, eligibility, search, margins, alpha spending, and budgets, then acquire at least four genuinely new paper-task pairs with untouched source maps, complete artifacts, assets, and scorers; run EffectSlice and all preregistered compact-skill baselines under identical branch budgets. On every held-out task whose F clears the beneficial-effect eligibility gate, a successful mechanism should produce an S_star with sealed M_tau(S_star)>0, no corrected contract or guardrail failure, and lower procedure count and measured local cost than F, while the baselines leave the sealed downstream effect gap outside [-epsilon,epsilon] more often. The single load-bearing variable is M_tau(S)=epsilon-sup{|g|: g in I_tau(S)}. As a negative control, permute discovery M_tau labels among same-size contract-passing candidates before selection, then evaluate the selected candidate on untouched confirmation seeds; its downstream paired effect gap should leave the equivalence margin and move toward the no-skill baseline more often than the unpermuted worker.
compute_budget: Upper-bound campaign: 12 tasks total (8 development + at least 4 genuinely new held-out), at most 16 dependency atoms and Q=24 adaptive candidates per task, two fresh discovery seeds for each S/F/B query branch, three sealed F/B eligibility seeds, and five confirmation seeds for F, B, S_star, up to 16 deletion neighbors, and four baselines. This is at most 144 discovery + 6 eligibility + 115 confirmation = 265 branch-runs per task, or 3,180 branch-runs total; at a preregistered pilot cap of 0.25 GPU-hour and $1.50 API per branch plus 15% rerun reserve, the full upper bound is approximately 38 GPU-days on 80GB-class GPUs + $5,500 API. If the pilot exceeds either per-branch cap, the campaign returns budget_infeasible rather than reducing confirmation seeds or changing Q after outcomes.

differentiation_from_lit.delta: Graph-of-Skills builds an executable dependency graph and retrieves dependency-complete skill bundles under a context budget, whereas EffectSlice first gates on a beneficial full-artifact effect and then seals a task-local paired effect-preservation certificate plus failed dependency-relative deletion evidence.

Abstract-level evidence indicates SkillRAE compiles compact grounded task contexts with evidence rescue, whereas EffectSlice fixes source-anchored procedure atoms and certifies their local irreducibility against the eligible complete artifact on untouched paired confirmation runs.

Abstract-level evidence indicates ClawTrace attributes cost and compiles preserve, prune, and repair patches, whereas EffectSlice requires a sealed beneficial-effect gate and corrected equivalence, contract, guardrail, and failed-removal certificates for one fixed task.

Anything2Skill compiles evidence-linked procedural contracts from external knowledge, whereas EffectSlice treats that compiled artifact as a fixed reference and certifies whether a frozen-granularity subset preserves its beneficial downstream effect on an independently locked task.

SkillFoundry mines, repairs, and validates executable scientific skills before downstream evaluation, whereas EffectSlice emits no reusable library and instead seals one eligibility-gated task-local effect certificate for a dependency-relative locally irreducible subset.

what_step_was_missed: ClawTrace would have needed to prove the complete skill has a beneficial paired effect first, freeze source-grounded dependency atoms before pruning, and use untouched confirmation runs to certify both effect equivalence of the retained slice and failure of every dependency-relative one-atom deletion.
